item.title: County Issues Code Blue Preparations for Extreme Cold Weather This Weekend
item.description: A warming station at 291 Chestnut Street, run by Catholic Charities of Delaware, Otsego and Schoharie Counties, is open on Code Blue-qualifying nights from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 a.m. the next morning. Due to the current extreme temperatures, however, officials said the warming station opened at 11 a.m. today, January 30, and will remain open the entire weekend until Monday morning, February 2.

item.title: In Memoriam: Jeff C. Seamon
item.description: Jeff C. Seamon, 63, of Richfield Springs, New York, passed away unexpectedly on January 23, 2026. Born March 8, 1962 in New Berlin, New York to Louis and Marie Seamon, he was the youngest son of nine children. He attended Richfield Springs Central School. Growing up on the family farm ignited his lifelong interest in agricultural and mechanical pursuits.

item.title: In Memoriam: Walter E. Wart
item.description: It is with deep sorrow and much love that we announce the passing of Walter E. Wart, beloved husband, father, and dear friend. Walter E. Wart, 54, of Hartwick, passed away on Friday, January 30, 2026 peacefully at home with his family at bedside.

item.title: In Memoriam: James S. Bridger
item.description: James S. Bridger, a native of Cooperstown known by many as Foxy or Jim, passed away late Saturday morning, January 24, 2026, at Bassett Medical Center in Cooperstown following a lengthy illness. He was 80. Born February 27, 1945 at the Mary Imogene Bassett Hospital in Cooperstown, Jim was the only child of Norman C. and Clara (Sprague) Bridger.

item.title: The Partial Observer: Activists Are Suppressing Research Into Gender-Affirming Care. It Has To Stop.
item.description: Evidence for the long-term safety and effectiveness of these interventions remains weak. Other countries—Finland, Sweden, the UK and New Zealand—have sharply restricted the availability of these interventions for minors. By contrast, in the U.S., scrutiny itself has become taboo. Researchers who challenge prevailing assumptions often face harassment.
